title: Reduced relative clauses
objectives: Recognise active and passive reduced relative clauses.
Form controlled reductions without changing the intended meaning.
Distinguish an ongoing passive from a completed passive description.

explanation.heading: Meaning and use
paragraphs: A reduced relative clause modifies a noun without using a full relative clause. ‘The people waiting outside can come in’ can correspond to ‘The people who are waiting outside can come in’. The -ing phrase identifies the people. ‘The documents signed yesterday are on the desk’ can correspond to ‘The documents that were signed yesterday are on the desk’.

Reduced clauses can make writing more concise, especially in descriptions and formal texts. They are not simply shorter versions of every relative clause. The time, aspect and meaning of the original clause must remain clear, and some reductions sound unnatural or change the intended meaning.

explanation.heading: Form
paragraphs: An -ing form can replace some active relative clauses, particularly when the clause describes an action in progress or a characteristic activity: ‘The people who are waiting outside’ becomes ‘the people waiting outside’. The noun being modified is understood as the performer of the activity.

A past participle can replace some passive relative clauses: ‘The documents that were signed yesterday’ becomes ‘the documents signed yesterday’. The documents received the action. In some contexts, being plus a participle can retain a passive action-in-progress meaning: ‘The road being repaired is closed’ describes an ongoing repair.

explanation.heading: Examples in context
paragraphs: Compare ‘The engineer repairing the machine is Ana’ with ‘The machine repaired yesterday is working’. The engineer performs the repair; the machine received an earlier repair. ‘The machine being repaired is not available’ focuses on an ongoing passive activity. These forms are not interchangeable if they change who performs or receives the action.

A reduced phrase normally follows the noun it modifies: ‘the students waiting outside’. It does not normally need a relative pronoun or a finite form of be: ‘the students waiting outside’, not ‘the students who waiting outside’. A full relative clause can still be clearer, especially when time or aspect would otherwise be ambiguous.

explanation.heading: Contrasts and common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not assume an -ing clause always means an action happening at the exact moment of speaking. ‘People working night shifts’ can describe a characteristic activity. Nor does a bare past participle always specify exactly when an action happened; context supplies the time.

Avoid reducing a clause if the resulting phrase would misrepresent the intended relationship. ‘The man who I saw’ cannot simply become ‘the man seeing’ when he was the person I saw: seeing would make him the performer. Keep the full clause or use a different wording that preserves the meaning. Some reduced forms have several possible interpretations, so exercises specify the intended relationship.

examples.sentence: The people waiting outside can come in.
examples.note: Waiting describes the people as performers of the activity.

examples.sentence: The documents signed yesterday are on the desk.
examples.note: Signed describes documents that received the earlier action.

examples.sentence: The road being repaired is closed.
examples.note: Being repaired presents an ongoing passive activity.

examples.sentence: The engineer repairing the machine is Ana.
The machine repaired yesterday is working.
People working night shifts need rest.
examples.note: Working can describe a characteristic activity.

examples.sentence: The people who are waiting outside can come in.
examples.note: The full relative clause can express the same intended relationship.

examples.sentence: The documents that were signed yesterday are on the desk.
examples.note: The full passive relative clause specifies the earlier action.

common_errors.incorrect: The students who waiting outside can enter.
common_errors.correct: The students waiting outside can enter.
common_errors.reason: The reduced -ing clause does not take who in this pattern.

common_errors.incorrect: The documents signing yesterday are on the desk.
common_errors.correct: The documents signed yesterday are on the desk.
common_errors.reason: Use a passive participle because the documents received the action.

common_errors.incorrect: The road being repair is closed.
common_errors.correct: The road being repaired is closed.
common_errors.reason: Use the past participle after being in this passive pattern.

summary: An -ing phrase can reduce some active relative clauses.
A past participle can reduce some passive relative clauses; being plus a participle can show passive progress.
Preserve the original subject, time and meaning when reducing a clause.

exercises.prompt: The people who are waiting outside can enter. Choose the reduction.
exercises.explanation: Waiting describes the people performing the ongoing action.

options.text: The people waited outside can enter.
The people who waiting outside can enter.
The people waiting outside can enter.
The people being waited outside can enter.

option_feedback.a: “The people waited outside can enter.” does not fit here. Waiting describes the people performing the ongoing action.
option_feedback.b: “The people who waiting outside can enter.” does not fit here. Waiting describes the people performing the ongoing action.
option_feedback.c: “The people waiting outside can enter.” fits here. Waiting describes the people performing the ongoing action.
option_feedback.d: “The people being waited outside can enter.” does not fit here. Waiting describes the people performing the ongoing action.

exercises.prompt: The documents that were signed yesterday are on the desk. Choose the reduction.
exercises.explanation: Signed describes the documents receiving the earlier action.

options.text: The documents signed yesterday are on the desk.
The documents signing yesterday are on the desk.
The documents who signed yesterday are on the desk.
The documents being sign yesterday are on the desk.

option_feedback.a: “The documents signed yesterday are on the desk.” fits here. Signed describes the documents receiving the earlier action.
option_feedback.b: “The documents signing yesterday are on the desk.” does not fit here. Signed describes the documents receiving the earlier action.
option_feedback.c: “The documents who signed yesterday are on the desk.” does not fit here. Signed describes the documents receiving the earlier action.
option_feedback.d: “The documents being sign yesterday are on the desk.” does not fit here. Signed describes the documents receiving the earlier action.

the road being repair
the road who repairs
the road being repaired

option_feedback.a: “the road repairing the workers” does not fit here. Being repaired presents the road as receiving an ongoing action.
option_feedback.b: “the road being repair” does not fit here. Being repaired presents the road as receiving an ongoing action.
option_feedback.c: “the road who repairs” does not fit here. Being repaired presents the road as receiving an ongoing action.
option_feedback.d: “the road being repaired” fits here. Being repaired presents the road as receiving an ongoing action.

options.text: the engineer repaired by the machine
the engineer repairing the machine
the engineer being repaired by the machine
the engineer repair yesterday

option_feedback.a: “the engineer repaired by the machine” does not fit here. Repairing describes the engineer as the performer.
option_feedback.b: “the engineer repairing the machine” fits here. Repairing describes the engineer as the performer.
option_feedback.c: “the engineer being repaired by the machine” does not fit here. Repairing describes the engineer as the performer.
option_feedback.d: “the engineer repair yesterday” does not fit here. Repairing describes the engineer as the performer.

option_feedback.b: “The man seeing by me was tall.” does not fit here. Who I saw identifies the man as the person seen.

option_feedback.d: “The man saw by I was tall.” does not fit here. Who I saw identifies the man as the person seen.
